rv.q: The placement of those titles, far above the actors’ heads on a set by Jessica Alexandra Cancino, fundamentally thwarts this fast-paced pageant, whose arc takes it from the Vilna Ghetto, in what is now Lithuania, to a displaced persons camp in Germany.
No other company does this kind of work, and it would be a shame to miss this moving and revelatory showcase of mostly forgotten songs that still embody the spirit of survival and resistance.
“Amid Falling Walls” can also be appreciated just as another artful and entertaining work of theater from the folks at folksbiene.
This captivating show, nearly all of it in Yiddish, will have you wiping away tears with one hand and clapping your knee with the other, even if you don’t know a brokhe from a bris.
Certainly, this production’s message of Jews’ resilience amid tragedy and sorrow is an appropriate message for events of the day.

cn.t: Critics praise this Yiddish musical revue for powerfully reviving songs from Holocaust ghettos and camps, finding it a moving act of remembrance that balances tears with moments of defiant humor and creativity amid darkness.
